strongFeatures: Airport search works by airport, city and IATA code.
Security side, room location, hours, wudu, women’s space and qibla appear consistently with sources and dates.
A compact airport board makes status and facilities comparable.
Unknowns remain explicit rather than appearing confirmed.
Visitors can copy an enquiry and follow the institution’s own feedback link; messages are sent by the visitor.
Planner, travel guidance and documented improvements provide useful follow-through.
hamzaIdentity.blendRecommendation: Retain navy/yellow wayfinding, trustworthy tabular facts and visitor-owned actions. Use Archivo consistently for the new interface and preserve Noto Naskh Arabic. Make the room the setting for a single clear search and arrival journey; do not reproduce every typeface merely because the original uses it.

duplicationReview.preserve: Do not duplicate these cards, silently update original room verification dates, or infer universal access from the examples below.

guidance.title: Ask a terminal ambassador for directions
guidance.text: Melbourne Airport directs unsure travellers to its Experience Ambassadors. The chaplaincy office is on Level 2 in Terminal 2; its phone is monitored around the clock.

source.title: Melbourne Airport — Find support from the airport chaplaincy
source.assessment: Full page opened; relevant sections are the chaplaincy location and Experience Ambassadors paragraph.

guidance.gap: The existing MEL record has two room locations and hours, but no human wayfinding fallback.
guidance.caveat: A continuously monitored phone does not mean the office is staffed continuously. This is Melbourne-specific advice.

guidance.place: University of Bristol — Woodland Prayer Rooms
guidance.title: Arrange card access before an evening visit
guidance.text: For 24-hour access to the prayer rooms at 21 Woodland Road, Bristol asks users to email the Multifaith Chaplaincy to activate their Ucard.

source.title: University of Bristol — Places to Worship
source.assessment: Full page opened; Woodland Prayer Rooms section explicitly specifies Ucard activation.

guidance.gap: Useful distinction between published opening hours and an access card that must first be enabled; not in current VisitInsights.
guidance.caveat: This page describes facilities for university students and staff. Do not imply public access or create a new directory record from this tip alone.

guidance.place: UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health
guidance.title: Keep shared rooms available for prayer
guidance.text: GOS ICH’s G01 prayer room at 30 Guilford Street is not bookable. Its guidance asks users to use the shoe shelves, avoid phones and laptops inside, and take personal belongings away.

source.title: UCL GOS ICH — Quiet rooms
source.assessment: Full page opened; room identity, booking policy, users and rules all explicit.

guidance.gap: Different room and purpose from existing UCL Pharmacy insight; adds shared-space etiquette and no-booking distinction.
guidance.caveat: Applies specifically to these GOS ICH rooms, not every UCL room. The page welcomes staff, students and visitors but does not detail building-entry procedure.

guidance.place: Ashford Hospital and St Peter’s Hospital, Surrey
guidance.title: A locked door may have a staffed access route
guidance.text: Both centres list daily opening from 08:00 to 18:00. The Trust says security staff can unlock them outside those hours when needed.

source.title: Ashford and St Peter’s Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust — Our Multi-Faith Centres
source.assessment: Full page opened; both centres have explicit hours and security-unlocking statement.

guidance.gap: Practical after-hours route beyond a bare closed/open label; absent from current hospital records and VisitInsights.
guidance.caveat: Do not label the rooms unconditionally open 24/7. Security assistance is an access process, not a guaranteed immediate entry time. Do not create new records from this tip alone.

guidance.title: Shared spaces cannot always be reserved
guidance.text: Zagreb’s airport prayer room is shared across faiths. Its official guidance says no group may reserve it or take exclusive use, and links to the airport map for its position.

source.title: Zagreb Airport — The Prayer Room
source.assessment: Full page opened; reservation restrictions and map link explicit.

guidance.gap: Clarifies shared-room expectations without inventing room-specific services; absent from current VisitInsights.
guidance.caveat: This rule is specific to Zagreb. The source does not state hours, security side, wudu provision or separate spaces; leave these unknown.

uiRecommendations: Use one short next-action card near access information, sourced to the exact institution: ask an ambassador, activate a card, or contact security. Keep it separate from formal room records.
Show conditional after-hours access distinctly from ordinary hours. Never convert an on-request access statement into an unconditional 24-hour badge.
Keep historical photo date and location visible; use authentic photos for place evidence and labelled generated artwork only for the room concept.

Use a coherent arrival sequence: locate the room, confirm eligibility/security side, check hours and facilities, then open the official map or instructions. This is presentation guidance, not a new factual rule.
